note: About as close to the stated ICP as this corpus gets on the commercial criteria. He owns three factories and five mines, mentions a yacht in passing, and restates both list prices himself without resistance — 'successful' and 'income' are unambiguous. 'good_to_great' is met almost verbatim; the rep names it back to him as 'it's not really about surviving, it's just becoming like top level, the next level.' 'not_deconditioned' is met emphatically: he windsurfed for two hours the morning of the call, plays basketball three times a week and runs half marathons at 50. The single miss is 'neglected_health', and it is a miss in the ICP's literal wording rather than a disqualifier — health is not the neglected area of his life, it is arguably the most attended area. That is the interesting finding here. The ICP is written to screen out people in crisis, and it does, but it does not describe the opposite tail: a prospect who is fitter than the programme's intended customer and is buying marginal athletic performance rather than a turnaround. He is a core-fit buyer for commercial purposes whose actual demand — peaking for a national championship — the offer was never shown to serve.
